edges.description: Transformed thymic epithelium recurrently acquires somatic TP53 inactivating mutations.
Transformed cells engage RTK signaling, including KIT.
Transformed thymic epithelial tumor cells upregulate PD-L1 to suppress antitumor T-cell responses.
Clonal expansion of transformed thymic epithelial cells in the thymus produces a prevascular (anterior) mediastinal mass.
Loss of CDK4/6 inhibition at the G1/S checkpoint drives dysregulated cell-cycle entry and proliferation.

edges.description: Loss of p53 checkpoint and pro-apoptotic control permits survival and continued cycling of genomically unstable carcinoma cells.
RTK signaling drives proliferative output in thymic carcinoma cells.
Uncontrolled proliferation precedes aggressive invasion and spread.
Direct invasion of the pericardium, pleura, and anterior chest wall produces chest pain.
Mediastinal airway, pulmonary, and vascular compression or infiltration causes dyspnea.
Tracheobronchial compression and pleural/pulmonary invasion trigger cough.
Invasion and seeding of the pleural space produce malignant or reactive pleural effusion.
Lymphatic dissemination of invasive thymic carcinoma produces mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
Locally advanced and metastatic tumor burden drives systemic catabolism and constitutional weight loss.
